transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-04
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jorge Alvarez (Redwood Security Eng), Markus Vogel (CTO, AegisHealth), Lisa Chen (Head of Security), Devon Park (SRE), Rina Patel (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick security & compliance deep dive focused on incident response (IR), business continuity / disaster recovery (BCDR), RTO/RPO targets, uptime/SLA expectations, and the escalation process (PagerDuty/runbooks/exec notifications). Customer wants concrete timelines and artifacts to present to their board and infosec committee.

Topics: SOC 2 / ISO status, RBAC/SSO & SAML, audit log retention and format, KMS/encryption, IR runbooks, BCDR testing cadence, RTO/RPO, SLA uptime and credits, escalation matrix and on-call rotations.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, we'll keep this focused. I'm Ethan from Redwood, AE on this deal. With me are Priya, our solutions engineer, and Jorge from security.
[00:18] Markus: Hi all. We're really keen to walk through IR and DR — specifically what we can expect for RTO/RPO and the escalation flow. We have an upcoming board audit and need concrete answers.
[00:33] Lisa: Also want to confirm how audit logs look, where they're stored, retention, and how Redwood integrates with our KMS.
[00:45] Priya: Great, quick agenda: IR runbook and PagerDuty, BCDR targets (RTO/RPO), SLA and uptime, and then gaps for SOC2/ISO. We'll surface logs/KMS examples. Not too formal, sorry if I jump around.
[01:02] Devon: Quick callout: our prod traffic is multi-region and we need < 60s tail latency goals. The SRE team cares about graceful failover and deterministic failback.
[01:18] Jorge: On the security side we'll cover notification timelines, who gets paged at what severity, and post-incident reporting. Our standard is initial page within 10 minutes for Sev1 and postmortem within 72 hours.
[01:35] Ethan: To set context, Redwood currently publishes a 99.9% SLA on hosted inference for standard tiers, and we have dedicated SLA options for enterprise with higher uptime and faster support SLAs. We'll map that against your requirements.
[01:50] Markus: 99.9% is fine as a baseline — what's the standard RTO you design for?
[02:01] Priya: For hosted multi-tenant endpoints we design for sub-5 minute detection and warm failover within 15 minutes for regional infra exhaustion but realistic customer-visible RTO varies by topology; for Dedicated or Private it's configurable. For BCDR we typically aim for an RPO of under 5 minutes with KV cache strategies, but again that depends on prefix caching and client-side replay tolerance.
[02:24] Lisa: Can you repeat the RPO? I think you said under 5 minutes but we need written guarantees.
[02:30] Jorge: Yeah, we'll capture that. Note: for private deployments where customer manages underlying storage we advise a documented RPO that matches their snapshot cadence — Redwood can enforce application-level checkpoints but persistent store recovery is customer-controlled.
[02:46] Devon: So if we run Dedicated, who owns the KMS keys for encrypted model artifacts?
[02:52] Priya: Two patterns: Redwood-managed KMS for hosted with envelope encryption, or customer-managed keys (CMK) in your cloud KMS or HSM for Dedicated/Private. When you use CMK, Redwood never stores the plaintext key — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and external HSM via standard integrations.
[03:12] Rina: For compliance we need to show key rotation policies and where audit logs are shipped.
[03:18] Jorge: Audit logs include request metadata, auth decisions, admin actions (role changes), and deployment events. We can stream logs to your tenant's S3/GCS or to a SIEM via syslog/HTTP exporter. Retention is configurable; default retention is 90 days in-hosted but we can extend to match your retention policy via add-on.
[03:37] Lisa: Is the audit log schema standardized? We must ingest it into our Splunk instance.
[03:42] Priya: Yes, we can provide JSON-formatted events with timestamps, request IDs, user/role, resource, and outcome. We'll share sample logs. Speaker misheard: sometimes "kv cache" may be transcribed as "kayv cache" in our docs but the actual logs label it as kv_cache.
[03:59] Markus: Walk me through an incident timeline — detection, initial responders, exec notification, regulatory notification?
[04:07] Jorge: Typical Sev1 timeline: detection automatically (monitoring/tracing alert) -> primary on-call (SRE/SE) paged immediately -> triage within 10 minutes -> if unresolved within 30 minutes escalate to on-call manager -> if 60+ minutes and service degraded externally, notify account exec and customer security lead; regulatory notification depends on data exposure triggers per contract and law. We have templates for customer-facing notifications and postmortems.
[04:33] Lisa: Do you publish an SLA credit table and mean time to recovery (MTTR) commitments?
[04:39] Ethan: Yes, we'll send the SLA PDF. For hosted 99.9% there is a credit table; Dedicated includes optional higher SLAs and faster support response times. MTTR targets are in the runbook but we prefer to propose testing to validate.
[04:54] Devon: About runbooks — are they public or redacted? We need to ensure no internal sensitive data is leaked when we share with our ops team and execs.
[05:03] Jorge: We provide a customer-facing runbook that redacts internal telemetry endpoints and internal IPs; it includes play-by-play steps, severity definitions, runbook owners, and rollback steps. Full internal runbooks are internal to Redwood.
[05:17] Markus: What about cross-region failover — is that automated or manual? We need deterministic failover with known RTO.
[05:25] Priya: For multi-region we have an active-active routing layer that can route around region failures for stateless inference; for stateful workloads we recommend Dedicated with cross-region replicas. Automated failover depends on your topology — for stateless it's near-instant routing; for stateful there is a handover process with replication lag considerations. We'll provide measured failover numbers from internal DR tests.
[05:47] Lisa: Any experience with compliance-driven DR tests? Boards ask for tabletop exercises and documented test results.
[05:54] Jorge: Yes, we run annual DR exercises and can support joint tabletop tests. We produce artifacts: test plan, run results, lessons learned, and follow-ups. We recommend quarterly tabletop for higher-risk customers.
[06:10] Ethan: Quick product note: we also offer a private VPC deployment where the control plane is customer-managed; in those cases most compliance responsibilities move to the customer but Redwood still supports the orchestration.
[06:21] Devon: In that model, do we get the same SLA?
[06:25] Ethan: SLA depends on who manages the infra. For fully customer-managed VPC, Redwood provides best-effort support and a platform contract; for private with Redwood-managed control plane we can offer enterprise SLAs. We'll map that in the contract.
[06:40] Markus: Okay, next: escalation matrix specifics — who gets paged and at what thresholds? We have a strict chain: SRE -> SRE lead -> Security -> CTO -> Exec. We need to know where Redwood fits.
[06:51] Jorge: Our recommended integration: primary on-call is Redwood SRE/SE depending on product tier; you can set dual-notification so both Redwood and your SRE are paged simultaneously. Severity mapping is configurable (e.g., error rate spike -> Sev2, full endpoint outage -> Sev1). We support PagerDuty and Opsgenie integrations and will provide the runbook mapping file.
[07:15] Lisa: Are there pre-authorized exec notification templates we can use for regulatory reporting?
[07:21] Priya: Yes, templated messages exist for Sev1 with redactions. They include timelines, impact, mitigation steps, and next steps. We also include the internal RCA template for postmortems.
[07:33] Markus: About legal/regulatory — what triggers a 72-hour breach notification?
[07:38] Jorge: That depends on whether PII or regulated PHI was exposed. Our IR playbook includes classification steps; if the incident meets your legal criteria we will assist with timelines. Contractually, notification obligations are spelled out in the Data Processing Agreement (DPA).
[07:56] Rina: Can you confirm data residency? We have EU patient data that must remain in EU.
[08:02] Priya: Yes, we support region pinning for model serving and storage. For EU-resident workloads we can configure regions and ensure logs and models stay in region for private/dedicated; hosted-tier may require the dedicated option depending on sensitivity. We'll include region-residency config examples.
[08:19] Lisa: For encryption at rest and in transit, are all keys rotated quarterly?
[08:24] Jorge: Key rotation cadence for Redwood-managed keys is 90 days by default; for CMKs you control rotation policies. We can produce a key-rotation certificate and timeline for auditors.
[08:36] Devon: On telemetry — does Redwood retain the KV cache contents in logs? That could be PII if prompts contain PHI.
[08:44] Priya: We try not to retain user prompts in cleartext in logs unless configured. There are explicit settings for prompt redaction and verbatim retention. For regulated data we recommend private deployments and strict retention policies.
[08:58] Speaker 4: (brief cross-talk, unclear)
[09:05] Markus: How do you test runbook effectiveness? Are there playbooks for simulated incidents?
[09:10] Jorge: We run simulated incidents (fire drills) where we trigger synthetic failures and verify detection, paging, escalation, and failover; we capture enlistment times and MTTR. We'll provide a sample test report.
[09:25] Ethan: To tie to your board ask: we'll provide a bundle — SOC2 Type II report, ISO roadmap, IR runbook, SLA docs, sample audit logs, and a DR test plan.
[09:37] Rina: Perfect. Can you state if Redwood has SOC2 Type II today?
[09:41] Jorge: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II for the control plane and is in progress for some connectors; ISO 27001 is targeted for Q3 2025. We'll attach certs and the latest auditor letter.
[09:56] Lisa: For evidence we want tangible dates — so please include audit period and assessor.
[10:01] Jorge: Yes, we'll include assessor names, testing period, and scope.
[10:07] Devon: SLA question again: are there scheduled maintenance windows and how are they announced?
[10:13] Ethan: Standard maintenance windows are announced 72 hours in advance for non-critical updates; emergency patches may be applied with immediate notice and an after-action note. For Dedicated customers you can nominate blackout windows.
[10:26] Markus: On the escalation front, who owns customer communication templates? Can our comms team edit them?
[10:32] Priya: We share templates which you can copy into your SRE runbooks and customize. We recommend joint runbook ownership for critical workflows.
[10:41] Lisa: On post-incident review — does Redwood permit joint RCA reviews with customer security teams?
[10:47] Jorge: Absolutely, joint RCAs are standard for enterprise customers. We set an initial internal timeline (72 hours to publish a draft postmortem) and then we collaborate on redactions and a final public postmortem if needed.
[11:00] Markus: We need to understand service dependencies — do you publish a dependency map (databases, 3rd party gateways) we can ingest?
[11:07] Priya: We can supply a dependency diagram and describe 3rd-party vendor impact. We also publish a compatibility matrix for model runtimes and kernel selection (note: transcription may show weird kernel names.).
[11:20] Devon: About ticketing and SLAs — how fast do you respond to Sev1 pages?
[11:25] Ethan: For enterprise Dedicated customers, initial response is 15 minutes and updates every 15 minutes until recovery. For hosted standard tier it's longer, which we'll document in the SLA.
[11:35] Rina: Will Redwood provide a runbook template we can run through in our next tabletop?
[11:39] Priya: Yes, we'll provide the template and help run the tabletop.
[11:44] Lisa: For the DR plan, what's your RTO for model-serving endpoints if the primary region is down?
[11:50] Priya: For stateless inference active-active, failover is typically < 120s at the routing level; for stateful cold-start models there's a longer cold-start penalty. For Dedicated with pre-warmed cross-region replicas we can get sub-10 minute RTOs with warmed model caches. We'll share measured numbers.
[12:07] Markus: We need specifics on RPO per workload class — batch embeddings vs low-latency chat.
[12:13] Jorge: For batch jobs acceptable RPO can be minutes to hours; for low-latency chat we recommend sub-5 minute RPO with continuous KV replication where possible.
[12:26] Devon: Any limits on audit log throughput or retention cost?
[12:31] Priya: There's a cost model for extended retention; large log throughput is supported via streaming to your infra. We'll include pricing examples.
[12:43] Ethan: Quick note — sometimes names get transcribed wrong in the automated export; you'll see Speaker tags like Speaker 2 in the raw.
[12:50] (brief pause)
[13:00] Markus: Let's go through an example scenario — a model-serving CPU exhaustion in eu-west-1 causing degraded responses. What happens?
[13:10] Priya: Monitoring triggers an autoscaling policy or a capacity failover; if capacity unavailable within policy window, route to dedicated fallback model or warm standby region. If that still fails, raise Sev1. The decision matrix is in the runbook.
[13:30] Lisa: What about data deletion requests during an incident? We have GDPR erasure requests that could be queued behind the incident.
[13:37] Jorge: Data deletion is processed via our data lifecycle API; we treat legal holds specially and will coordinate with your compliance team. We'll also provide proof of deletion artifacts tied to request IDs.
[13:53] Devon: For escalation, do we have a joint war room channel?
[13:58] Ethan: Yes, we encourage a shared Slack/Teams channel and a joint Zoom war room for Sev1s. We can generate that channel and invite your SRE and security folks on escalation.
[14:10] Rina: About tabletop testing — can Redwood facilitate and act as a simulated partner (injecting faults)?
[14:16] Jorge: Yes, we can both facilitate and participate. We'll script scenarios and provide a facilitator to run the exercise.
[14:26] Lisa: Do you have specific executive escalation thresholds (e.g., 2 hours of degraded service)?
[14:32] Priya: We recommend an exec notification at 60 minutes for widespread customer impact; that mapping is configurable in the contract.
[14:41] Markus: One last thing — do we get a service availability dashboard and historical uptime?
[14:47] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route/model dashboards with latency and error metrics; historical uptime and incident timelines are available. We'll grant view-only access for your ops and security.
[14:59] (wrap-up)
[15:05] Ethan: To recap next steps: we'll send the IR runbook, SLA docs, SOC2 artifacts, sample audit logs, and a proposed DR tabletop schedule. We will also include a proposed RTO/RPO matrix for your review.
[15:18] Markus: Sounds good. We'll confirm target RTO/RPO and blackout windows by Friday.
[15:24] Rina: We'll also send any region-specific residency requirements.
[15:28] Priya: Great, we'll action those items and follow up with calendar invites.
[15:33] Ethan: Thanks everyone, we'll send the bundle by Friday.
[15:36] End of call.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (speaker tags, acronyms). Some technical terms may appear as similar-sounding words in auto transcript.

Attachments referenced during call: SLA_Pricing.pdf (link), SOC2_Summary.pdf (link), IR_Runbook_sample.docx (link), DR_Tabletop_Template.xlsx (link).

Explicit next steps (in-text): Redwood to provide artifacts and schedule DR tabletop. Customer to confirm RTO/RPO and residency constraints.
